questions.question: The Right to Information Act is a good example of a law and it has more chances of working because:

options.text: it acts as an enemy of democracy
it supplements laws that encourage corruption
it empowers people to find out what is happening in the government

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**it empowers people to find out what is happening in the government.**__

__
 
• ** Right to Information Act 2005** mandates timely response to citizen requests for government information
 
• It is an initiative taken by the** Department of Personnel and Training, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances** 
 
• Anybody can seek information from any government organization across the Indian territory
 
• For matters involving the**; Life of Liberty '**of a person the time limit for the public information officer to provide information** is 2 days**

• RTI or **Right to Information Act is a fundamental right** and is an aspect o**f Article 19 (1)(a)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Right to Information** replaced the Freedom of Information Act, 2002**.
 
• The idea of RTI in India brainchild of former PM, **V.P. Singh in 1990.**
 
• The first grassroots campaign for the introduction of RTI started by** Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) in 1994**

questions.question: Different crops grown in alternate rows is an example of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Intercropping.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Intercropping involves growing** two or more crops simultaneously** on the** same fiel**d but they are** not mixed with each other.**
 
• They have grown in inset patterns.
 
• This **pattern prevents pests and diseases **to spread in all the plants of one crop and following in a given area.
 
• Various types of intercropping were known and presumably employed in ancient** Greece about 300 B.C​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****

__
 
• **Three types of cropping patterns**.

 
 
• Cropping Patterns**-Mixed Cropping**,** Intercropping**, **Crop Rotation**
 
• mix cropping-Mixed cropping, including intercropping, is the oldest form of systemized agricultural production and involves the growing of two or more species or cultivars of the same species simultaneously in the same field
 
• Crop rotation is defined as a “system of growing different kinds of crops in recurrent succession on the same land”
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• ** Three main types of crop**s.

 
 
• **Kharif crop**s- Grown in June- July, e.g., rice, cotton
 
• **Rabi crops-** Grown in October-November, e.g., wheat, potato
 
• **Zaid crops**- Grown between March- June, e.g., cucumber, pumpkin

questions.concept: Ecology and Functions of an ecosystem
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an abiotic component of the eco system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Living Organisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ecosystem**- The word Ecosystem was termed by 'Arthur Tansley' which means an interaction that occurs between Biotic and Abiotic components.
 
• The ecosystem is divided into two components Biotic and Abiotic components.
 
• **Abiotic components** consist of **Sunlight, oxygen, moisture, minerals, temperature, soil and water**.
 
• **Biotic components **consist of **Living organisms which are Plants (Producers) and Animals (Consumers)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/377faffe87f801fad37875fa8fe3fd5faa70648e1d3407f7e9052989a44ae655.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c829f5ca45562d2fd6ae56d8048d2693ba38c47b6c136e3a68efc5475407cb0d.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Producers**
 **Consumers**
 
 

 They are also called autotrophs.
 They are also known as Heterotropes
 
 

 An autotroph is an organism that can produce its own food in presence of sunlight or with the help of chemicals.
 Heterotrophs are animals which feed on other living organisms.
 
 

 They can perform photosynthesis and chemosynthesis to prepare food.
 They are further divided into Herbivores, carnivores and Omnivores.
 
 

 
 
Photosynthesis is done in the presence of sunlight by terrestrial and water plants (depth of 200 m).

 
Chemosynthesis is done in absence of sunlight by plants living in deep oceans.

 
 
 
Herbivores are animals which feed on plants.

 
Carnivores are animals which feed on other animals.

 
Omnivores are animals which eat both plants and animals.

questions.question: ________ is secreted by the pineal gland.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Melatonin**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Melatonin **is secreted by **Pineal Gland.**

 
 
• It is involved in the regulation of biological rhythms of the body and sleep.
 
• It is usually secreted in darkness hence also known as **"Dracula of Hormones".**
 
• Sometimes it can be consumed from external sources by mouth to adjust the body's internal clock, as well as its external supplements.
 
 
 
• **The pineal Gland is situated in the middle of the human brain and is the major site of the body's melatonin.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Progesterone **hormone is released during the course of pregnancy hence also known as pregnancy hormone.

 
 
• It inhibits the contraction of the uterus so that pregnancy can be sustained.
 
 
 
• **Epinephrine **also known as **Adrenaline, **is a hormone produced by adrenal glands and the small number of neurons in the medulla oblongata.
 
 
• It relaxes muscles in the airways and tightens the blood vessels.
 
 
 
• ​**Insulin** is a hormone secreted by the pancreas.
 
 
• It controls the amount of glucose in the bloodstream at any given moment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4199a6c1ee1ff75ded74ce27bffb2a031468140c73826129cc7d759f482b5158.png]

questions.question: Which of the following is non-justiciable in nature in Indian Constitution?

options.text: Equality of law and equal protection of law
Protection with respect to conviction of offences
Equal justice and free legal aid

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Equal justice and free legal aid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39A** of the Indian constitution deals with **Equal justice and free legal aid to the poor**.

 
 
• ​It is mentioned in the **Directive Principle Of State Policy** in** Part IV of the Constitution**.
 
• As the Directive Principle Of State Policy is a** non-enforceable and non-justiceable** part of the constitution.
 
• This means that they are **not legally enforceable by the court on their violation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 14** of the Indian Constitution states that **Equality of the law and equal protection of the law** which mean **all** **people are equal in front of the law**.
 
• **Article 20** of the Indian Constitution states the **Protection with respect to conviction of offenses**.
 
• **Article 26** of the Indian constitution provides** Freedom to manage religious affairs**.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Saila dance form is performed in the state of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points____ **__

__
 
• The Saila dance is a folk dance and is performed during the post-harvest season.
 
• Saila is a stick dance that is famous among the people of Sarguja, Chhindwara, and Baitul districts of Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other folk dances of Chattisgarh:**

 
 
• **Karma Dance- **This dance form marks the end of the rainy season and the advent of spring.
 
• **Suga Nacha- **Usually called a parrot dance, it is performed during Goura’s wedding.
 
• **Pandavani- **Portray the account of Pandavas, the main characters of an epic battle.
 
• **Panthi Dance- **It is a prominent custom of the Satnami community of Chhattisgarh.
 
 
• The community celebrates the anniversary of the birth of Guru Ghasidas in Maghi Purnima.
 
 
 
• **Rahas Dance**- The Rahas dance is performed during festivals in Chattisgarh.
 
 
• It is an important folk dance in the Dhamtari district of the state.

questions.question: To which nation does swimmer Gaurika Singh, who was the youngest athlete in Rio Olympics 2016, belong to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Nepal's swimming sensation **Gaurika Singh** was the youngest athlete to compete in the last Olympic Games in Rio held in 2016.
 
• She holds a record of winning 4 gold medals in a season of the South Asian games held in Nepal in 2019.
 
• She won two silver and three bronze medals for swimming at the 2016 South Asian Games.
 
• She also participated in 2016, Summer Olympics in the Women's 100 Meter backstroke.
 
• She is also a goodwill brand ambassador of the Shanti Education Initiative Nepal.
